clue.text: They importuned old sailors

parts.note: importuned suggests nagging pestering, but these bands pressed men forcibly into naval service in former times

explanation.surface: A description of people who pestered retired seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Importuned' hints at pressing someone, which is exactly what these gangs did to men they forced into the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical bands that forcibly conscripted men to serve as sailors in the navy.

clue.text: Medicine ball?

definitions.meaning: a tablet of medicine to swallow
a small round ball, a dated slang term also used for a ball in sport

explanation.definitionFit: A tablet of medication, and informally any small round ball, especially in sport.

clue.text: Battle to establish a male line?

indicators.note: establishing something means setting it up afresh, so these letters are rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: Wondering what fight could found a dynasty of men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to establish' rearranges A MALE LINE into the name of the 1942 North African battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous Second World War engagement in Egypt, fought in 1942.

clue.text: Measures ladder

definitions.meaning: actions taken, as in taking ... to fix something
a folding stepladder is often simply called by this name

explanation.definitionFit: Actions taken towards a goal, and a short folding ladder used indoors.

clue.text: Attached to a refined redhead

indicators.note: something refined has been processed and reworked, so the word's letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone fond of a cultured woman with red hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refined' rearranges REDHEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuck fast or joined to something is a direct synonym.

clue.text: It is not proverbially indicative of gold

definitions.text: It is not proverbially indicative of gold

parts.words: It is not proverbially indicative of gold
parts.note: refers to the proverb that all that shines in this way is not gold, using the old verb form

explanation.surface: A remark about a saying concerning gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb runs 'All that glisters is not gold'; the old verb meaning to sparkle is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic verb meaning to sparkle, from the proverb about appearances deceiving.

clue.text: They may hold one in affection

definitions.text: They may hold one in affection

parts.words: They may hold one in affection
parts.note: reads as people being fond of someone, but describes the limbs used to embrace a loved one

explanation.surface: Seems to describe people who are fond of somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase about affection sounds like liking someone; literally, an embrace grips a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbs used to hug a person in an affectionate embrace.

clue.text: Tears right as one finishes

parts.note: a person finishes, that is, ends

explanation.surface: Someone crying at the moment they complete something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' suggests crying, but it is the verb meaning rips.
explanation.definitionFit: Rips or tears apart is the sense of this verb.

clue.text: Back the winner-not the winner!

parts.note: to back a proposal is to second it
the winner is the best

explanation.surface: Advice to support the victor, contradicted at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like a betting instruction but means support, as in seconding a motion.
explanation.definitionFit: Runner-up or inferior to the top choice, hence not the victor.

clue.text: Begin an unusual run as top of the bill

parts.note: to begin is to start

indicators.note: an unusual version of the word is an altered arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: An athlete whose strange run makes them headline act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges RUN into URN.
explanation.definitionFit: The main performer billed first in a variety show or programme.

clue.text: Set out for a holiday

explanation.definitionFit: To depart, and also authorised time away from work or duty.

clue.text: It's meant to stimulate capital growth

definitions.text: It's meant to stimulate capital growth

parts.words: It's meant to stimulate capital growth
parts.note: capital growth suggests investment, but capital here is the head and growth is what sprouts on it

explanation.surface: Sounds like a financial policy to boost investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' means the head (Latin caput), so the growth is hair, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotion applied to the scalp, supposedly to encourage hair to grow.

clue.text: It was once the talk of India

definitions.text: It was once the talk of India

parts.words: It was once the talk of India
parts.note: talk of the town suggests gossip, but here talk means the language spoken there long ago

explanation.surface: Something that was formerly much discussed across India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The talk of' suggests gossip; it means the classical language of ancient India.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient classical language of India, now used mainly in religious texts.

clue.text: Schoolmaster returned to measure up

indicators.note: returned means the word is turned back and read backwards

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir
EN is a printer's measure of width

explanation.surface: A teacher came back to take measurements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses SIR to RIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Having got up or ascended, as in the sun has risen and is up.

clue.text: One bound to learn his craft

definitions.text: One bound to learn his craft

parts.words: One bound to learn his craft
parts.note: bound reads as certain to, but means bound by indentures to a master while training in a trade

explanation.surface: Someone destined to master a skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' suggests 'sure to', but traditionally a trainee was bound by indenture to a master.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee indentured to a skilled worker to learn a trade.

clue.text: Begs newspaperman who appears delighted

parts.note: begs are requests or appeals
ED is short for editor, a newspaperman

explanation.surface: A journalist who looks happy while begging.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad or delighted is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Left — that's ominous

definitions.meaning: Latin and heraldic word for the left-hand side

explanation.definitionFit: Heraldic left-hand side, and also threatening or menacing in tone.

clue.text: Fool might use this? Nonsense!

definitions.meaning: a fool is a creamy fruit dessert, often made with this stalk
a word for meaningless chatter, also what extras murmur on stage

explanation.definitionFit: A plant whose stalks go in a fruit fool dessert, and a word for babble or nonsense.

clue.text: A channel swimmer accepts kiss from great man in history

indicators.note: accepts means taking another piece inside

parts.note: Leander of Greek legend swam the Hellespont channel nightly to Hero
X is the symbol for a kiss

explanation.surface: A cross-channel swimmer welcoming a kiss from a historic figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The channel is the Hellespont, not the English Channel; 'accepts' puts X inside LEANDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great, the Macedonian conqueror, is a famous figure of history.

clue.text: Meet and collide

explanation.definitionFit: To meet by chance, or to crash into in a vehicle.

clue.text: Make no allowance in a speech

parts.note: O looks like zero, meaning no
a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: A speaker refusing to make concessions in an address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make no allowance' suggests being strict; split it as O plus RATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal public speech or address.

clue.text: Beats soundly in game that's child's play

indicators.note: soundly here signals a word that sounds like another when spoken

parts.note: beats an opponent, conquers them

explanation.surface: Someone trouncing others in a game for children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' seems to mean thoroughly, but signals the homophone. CONKERS is a British children's game of striking horse chestnuts on strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional British playground game with horse chestnuts on strings.

clue.text: On reflection, it's a great help for night drivers

definitions.text: On reflection, it's a great help for night drivers

parts.words: On reflection, it's a great help for night drivers
parts.note: on reflection reads as thinking again, but these road studs literally reflect headlights

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, something useful for motorists after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' sounds like 'having thought again'; these road studs work by reflecting headlights.
explanation.definitionFit: Reflective road studs that mark lanes for motorists at night.

clue.text: They may be held in revulsion

definitions.text: They may be held in revulsion

parts.words: They may be held in revulsion
parts.note: held in revulsion sounds like being loathed, but people literally pinch them against a bad smell

explanation.surface: Things people regard with disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held in revulsion' suggests loathing; literally one holds one's nose at a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: Facial features that people pinch shut when faced with something smelly.

clue.text: Take off one's football kit

explanation.definitionFit: To undress, and also a team's colours worn by footballers.

clue.text: Well, it pushes up water rates in a disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in ruins and disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A complaint that water bills have risen in a catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' rearranges RATES IN A. 'Well' looks like a sentence opener but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A well where pressure forces groundwater up without pumping.

clue.text: Start court proceedings

parts.note: suggests launching a lawsuit, but describes beginning a point on a tennis court

explanation.surface: Seems to mean launching legal action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests law; it is a tennis court, where each point begins this way (and a writ is also so delivered).
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, the stroke that starts play on court; also to deliver a writ.

clue.text: We hear repaired shoes have been disposed of

indicators.note: we hear signals a word that sounds the same when spoken

parts.note: shoes repaired with new soles have been soled

explanation.surface: Gossip that mended footwear has been got rid of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' signals the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Got rid of in exchange for money is a sense of the word.

clue.text: Realise it is translated into Hebrew

indicators.note: translating converts words into another form, so these letters are converted to a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to render a phrase into the Hebrew language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges REALISE IT. 'Hebrew' looks like a language but means a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the ancient Hebrew people.

clue.text: Set for one road diversion

indicators.note: a diversion sends traffic a different way, so these letters take a different route

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A traffic diversion sign set up on a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diversion' rearranges I and ROAD. 'Set' is a receiver, as in a wireless set.
explanation.definitionFit: A receiving set or wireless is an example of an apparatus called a set.

clue.text: Spot thought reading at a yard

parts.note: ESP is extrasensory perception, as in mind reading

explanation.surface: Seeing telepathy demonstrated in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch sight of or spot something is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Render duet badly but not put off

indicators.note: something done badly is messed up, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A pair perform poorly but carry on regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges RENDER DUET.
explanation.definitionFit: Not deterred or discouraged, carrying on regardless.
